Indra OCR Pipeline vs. ABBYY FineReader Benchmark

Comprehensive quantitative evaluation, automated lexical validity scoring, and spatial bounding-box alignment analysis across 7712 historical digital archive pages.

AI Executive Verdict Automated Quality Assurance Assessment
Across 7,712 historical pages and 1,809,905 recognized word tokens, the Indra OCR benchmark reveals an ultra-fast CPU engine (~8–12 pages/second in multi-process worker pools) that excels on clean, standard printed typography, but exhibits significant degradation on historical microfilm reels. While modern and standardized printed works show strong consensus (93.0% clean text concordance and 0.958 character similarity on Annuals), archive-wide concordance drops to 58.3% due to low contrast and faded ink in Heritage reels. Consequently, legacy ABBYY FineReader maintains a decisive quality advantage on degraded stock (10.8% overall QA win rate for Indra vs 89.2% for ABBYY), positioning Indra primarily as a rapid triage and clean-stock engine.
📘 Parity on Clean Print (Annuals: 93.0% Concordance): On standardized monograph and yearbook typography, Indra matches commercial quality with 93.0% clean concordance, 89.7% exact match, and 94.6% spatial alignment. For well-lit, non-degraded book collections, it reliably delivers publication-grade text extraction.
⚠️ Heritage Microfilm Degradation (54.7% Concordance, 9.7% QA Win): Indra struggled across 6,951 archival microfilm pages. Lacking adaptive CLAHE filtering, contrast normalization, and morphological stroke reconnection, it suffered on low-contrast ink, bleed-through, and microfilm glare—conceding 187,306 word disputes to ABBYY versus 20,219 Indra wins.
📰 Newspaper Layout & Arbitration (23.9% Win Rate): On high-density multi-column broadsheets, 3×2 quadrant tiling prevented truncated text lines, but complex reading order arbitration and micro-font resolution lagged behind ABBYY (1,952 vs 6,218 valid word wins, 23.9%), indicating broadsheets require specialized column segmentation.
⚡ CPU Throughput & Zero-GPU Footprint (~8–12 pgs/s): Indra's defining operational advantage is compute efficiency. Running on lightweight ONNX runtimes with ProcessPoolExecutor, it achieves 0.1–0.6s latency per page without requiring GPU VRAM, enabling economical high-throughput batching on standard CPU servers.

Clean Concordance ⓘ Clean Text Concordance

Spatial vs Concordance: Spatial Alignment checks where words are on the page, regardless of character agreement. Concordance checks what the words say.

Page / Item Name ⓘ Page / Item Name
Unique digital archive page stem. Click "Open Viewer →" in the Action column to inspect bounding boxes and side-by-side diffs.
 ▲ 		Collection ⓘ Collection
Publication category or archive sub-collection (e.g. Newspapers, Annuals, Heritage Microfilms). Filterable via dropdown.
 ⇕ 		Words: P / B (Delta) ⓘ Total Words & Delta
P = Pipeline (Indra) words, B = Benchmark (ABBYY) words, and (Delta) = P − B.
• Positive (+): Indra extracted more words (higher recall in fine print/captions).
• Negative (−): ABBYY extracted more words.
Click column header to sort by lowest delta (Indra fewer) or highest.
⇕ 		Spatial Align ⓘ Spatial Alignment (Box Overlap)
Measures whether Indra and ABBYY detected words in the same physical coordinate positions on the page, regardless of character recognition.
Spatial vs Concordance:
• Spatial Alignment tests WHERE words are located (box overlap IoU ≥ 0.25).
• Concordance tests WHAT the text characters say.
Both can find a box at the exact same coordinates (100% spatial align) even if they read different words.
⇕ 		Concordance ⓘ Clean Text Concordance
Character-level agreement between Indra and ABBYY for spatially matched words (normalized for punctuation and case).
• ≥ 90% (Green): High consensus; both engines agree.
• 80% – 90% (Yellow): Moderate agreement.
• < 80% (Red): Divergence; manual review suggested.
Key Point: Tests text character correctness rather than box coordinates.
⇕ 		Indra QA Win ⓘ Indra QA Win Rate
Automated dictionary validation on disputed words. Tests candidate words against English and French lexicons.
• Indra Win: Indra produced a valid real word while ABBYY produced OCR noise.
• ABBYY Win: ABBYY produced a valid real word while Indra failed.
Win Rate = Indra Wins ÷ (Indra Wins + ABBYY Wins).
⇕ 		Diffs ⓘ Discrepancy Count
Total number of word boxes where Indra and ABBYY disagree on the text characters.
Pages with high diff counts usually have degraded historical print or tight newspaper columns that benefit from side-by-side inspection.
⇕ 		Action ⓘ Interactive Viewer
Opens the synchronized interactive side-by-side zoomable visual viewer for in-depth inspection and manual adjudication.
